[34mInvestigated:[0m JSONStorage in tinydb/storages.py forwards its **kwargs to json.dumps on every write. The existing test_json_kwargs in tests/test_storages.py passes sort_keys=True explicitly, so it never tests the new default. The earlier sort_keys attempt was reverted after json.dumps raised TypeError on a dict mixing int and str keys.

[33mLearned:[0m With sort_keys=True, json.dumps raises TypeError when a dict mixes int and str keys. Passing sort_keys=False keeps insertion order, and int keys read back as strings, which is standard JSON behavior. The full suite runs with python -m pytest -c /dev/null tests because pytest.ini references unavailable coverage options.

[32mCompleted:[0m JSONStorage.__init__ records whether sort_keys was given. JSONStorage.write uses sort_keys=True by default and falls back to insertion order on TypeError, while an explicit sort_keys argument is used as given. The class docstring documents the default, the opt-out, and the fallback. Three tests were added to tests/test_storages.py covering the sorted default, the sort_keys=False opt-out, and mixed-key handling. An Unreleased entry was added to docs/changelog.rst. The full suite passes with 231 tests, and test_storages.py passes with 17 tests. Git status shows three modified files: tinydb/storages.py, tests/test_storages.py, and docs/changelog.rst. Nothing is committed.

[35mNext Steps:[0m No further work is in progress. The changes are uncommitted and the suite is passing.

[36mNotes:[0m The mixed-key fallback writes such documents unsorted, so their diffs can still be noisy. A stricter alternative would stringify keys before sorting, which was not pursued in this session. The fallback also catches unrelated TypeErrors from the serializer and re-raises them on the retry.
